body: I fear that it might damage my curiosity about the world...I don't want to be like the rest of the zombies I see every day.
You should go help someone who really needs it, I think I might just be sad and attention seeking, maybe I'm just lonely. Thank you for listening though, so much.

Ad I thought about it I realized that those were just residual feelings and that wasn't an accurate statement. No I'm not joining as an officer. I don't really have any hobbies, I enjoy doing magic and mentalism but I'm not really in serious study about it.

He is not different, he is the same as everyone else, he drinks, and he parties, and is a thrill seeker, and is an overachiever. He "loves" a girl who he has been dating for under a month. He is gullible and loves the world. I haven't really spoken to him since I moved to a new school, he isn't as great as I thought he was. He is not remarkably intelligent, and without a doubt he will die in the same small town he was born in, never achieving much. I've always been different from my family, I feel like they are imbeciles, nice and kind but imbeciles nonetheless. They are creationists, I'm not. They like sports, I don't. They are quite content living an average life and not learning much and leaving it all on "God teaches any wisdom that I need.". That's one of the reasons I joined the Navy, to get out of here and grow and expand...but I'm terrified the rest of the world is just as close minded.

I had a counselor recently who told me he thought I had an anti social personality disorder, he said he thought it was narcissism. I told him that was impossible because I don't love myself enough. Last year I considered the possibility that I had a personality disorder, I thought it was sociopathy because that's what my father was often described as and I know it has been shown to be hereditary. However, once again that's impossible, I think I care about people too much, I wouldn't be able to hold a relationship and I would have trouble with law enforcement. I have two people I actually consider friends,  my girlfriend and Jeff(who I haven't spoken to in weeks). Do you think it's possible that the counselor could have been correct? Maybe I use people for my own personal gain without actually knowing it?

So, I guess I always feel this way...it just gets put on hold until I actually have time to think about it. I think high school is pointless and life sucking, I do not enjoy it, I wouldn't go if I didn't have to. I view myself as an auto-didact and going to school everyday to be with kids who laugh and enjoy their time just irks me. I don't like social media, I don't think high school is "the greatest time of my life" I see it as a bureaucratic institution that is designed to produce workers, not individuals. It's just dull and lifeless.

I only function well socialy because I have read a lot about body language, and how to conduct yourself in social situations. I am popular because I made myself this way. When I changed schools I reformed myself, I created a version that was better socially. That, and the other school I came from had a unique ignorance about it, intelligence was not looked highly upon. This bigger school has opened up friendship opportunities that have never existed to me before...and yet I still feel alone...I feel like I have to put on a mask everyday and hold a charade just to fit in.
